thread:
Alex Chen: :rotating_light: seeing widespread 503s from Dedicated in us-west-2. Root appears to be the commit-capacity admission controller entering a lockout. Impacting customers on reserved pools.
Maria Gonzalez: which pool(s)? any metrics? send top-level logs/snapshots pls
Alex Chen: affected pools: commit-usw2-a and commit-usw2-b. spikes started ~1720456600. posting short sample from adm-controller:
```
[1720456661] ERROR admission: lockout=true inflight=243 max_capacity=250 drop_rate=0.98 backlog=180
[1720456670] WARN kvcache: memory_pressure=0.92 reclaim_attempts=3
[1720456678] INFO router: fallback_disabled=true
```
Maria Gonzalez: hmm kvcache memory_pressure > 0.9 is suspicious. Did a model hotload just happen on those nodes?
Dan S: we rotated a checkpoint for model-7b-opt at 1720456605 in commit-usw2-b. It spikes kv cache while warming. Should have warmed on spare nodes but looks like routing sent live traffic immediately.
ops-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-admission-lockout (us-west-2) — 95% of requests returned 503 between 1720456670 and 1720456740. Linked runbook: /runbooks/dedicated/admission-lockout
Priya Patel: customer comm? we should notify the small set of affected customers and share mitigation plan. I'll draft a note.
Alex Chen: immediate mitigations I'm rolling now:
- lower admission.max_inflight from 250 -> 120 to force backpressure earlier (prevents pileup)
- enable soft-fallback for tier=enterprise -> route to hosted for critical keys
- kill the warm job on commit-usw2-b and drain to spare nodes

Maria Gonzalez: config snippet?
Alex Chen: here's the quick change I applied:
```
admission:
  max_inflight: 120
  backpressure_threshold: 0.6
  soft_fallback: true
```
Dan S: after lowering max_inflight we're seeing inflight drop to ~110 and 503s drop. queue backlog has gone from 180 -> 22 in ~3m.
ops-bot: [METRICS SNAPSHOT]
- commit-usw2-a inflight: 98
- commit-usw2-b inflight: 112
- queue_length_total: 22
- 503_rate: 1.2% (was 18%)
Priya Patel: draft notice for affected customers: "We're investigating increased errors for Dedicated in us-west-2. We have temporarily routed critical traffic to Redwood Hosted and are throttling non-critical requests to stabilize. Expect ongoing improvements; we'll follow up with root cause and timeline." ok to send?
Maria Gonzalez: yes, send to the 7 affected accounts. add the workaround to their ticket: enable hosted-fallback flag.
Alex Chen: long-term followups (I'll own):
- add warm-on-spare gating so newly loaded model checkpoints don't receive production traffic until kvcache < 0.6
- automated rollback if kvcache pressure > 0.85 for > 2m
- lower default max_inflight for commit pools by 15%

Dan S: also look at router affinity so warm nodes get no live traffic for at least 5m post-load.
Priya Patel: sent notice to customers + created support tickets. tagging legal for SLA review.
Alex Chen: TL;DR: admission controller entered lockout due to kvcache memory pressure after model warm + routing misstep. mitigations applied (reduced inflight, enabled soft-fallback, drained warm job). 503s dropping, monitoring to confirm stability. action items created.
Maria Gonzalez: :thumbsup: please add postmortem link when ready and signal if we need a customer-level credit.
ops-bot: [INCIDENT UPDATE] status=stabilized, incident_id=INC-2026-0147, severity=high, assigned=Alex Chen/Dan S
